source_row.rationale: Current best practice for indwelling urinary catheter management emphasizes regularly reassessing the ongoing clinical necessity of the catheter (often through daily nursing/provider review or a nurse-driven removal protocol) and removing it as soon as it is no longer indicated, since prolonged catheter duration is the single most significant risk factor for catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI).
source_row.source_detail: Importance of Prompt Catheter Removal When No Longer Needed

source_row.stem: A nurse reviews a client's plan of care and notes an indwelling urinary catheter has been in place for several days without a clearly documented ongoing indication, and a colleague suggests it's simplest to just leave it until the physician happens to mention removing it.
